chunks: And by this chain, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who benefits from wealth, he said: 'He does not purify it (pay Zakat) until a year passes over it.'
ai.seo_question: When is Zakat due on wealth that is spent or used before a full year passes?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted via Safwan ibn Yahya, clarifies the condition of 'Hawl' (lunar year) for Zakat on newly acquired wealth, specifically addressing cases where wealth is spent or utilized before a full year elapses. It establishes that Zakat is not obligatory until the wealth remains in the owner's possession for a complete lunar cycle, a principle central to Shia fiqh regarding the timing of Zakat obligations. This ruling ensures that temporary holdings or rapidly circulating capital are not prematurely subject to the tax, aligning with the broader jurisprudential consensus on the necessity of sustained ownership.
